title: Avoid infinite componentDidUpdate loop when scrolling event log
answers: Why does scrolling the mitmweb event log trigger 'Maximum update depth exceeded'?
How to prevent infinite re-render loops in mitmweb virtualized lists?
What causes the event log to crash React when expanded and scrolled?
body:
Symptom: Expanding and scrolling the mitmweb event log throws React error "Maximum update depth exceeded".
Root cause: web/src/js/components/EventLog/EventList.tsx:EventLogList.componentDidUpdate called onViewportUpdate unconditionally, causing setState to fire repeatedly when variable row heights were measured.
Fix pattern: Gate onViewportUpdate calls in componentDidUpdate behind prop equality checks (prevProps.events !== this.props.events || prevProps.rowHeight !== this.props.rowHeight).
Constraints: Applies to virtual-scrolling components measuring dynamic row heights (such as EventLogList and FlowTable); scrolling, window resizing, and initial mounts must still handle viewport updates via dedicated listeners.
applies: Virtual scroll components in mitmweb that measure row heights dynamically
says: Scrolling through the event log panel crashes the web interface with an error.
The browser tab freezes completely whenever I expand and scroll the event log.
Expanding the event viewer and scrolling down causes the entire page to crash.
Prevent the web console from freezing when viewing long event history logs.
